key_insight: DeepONet trunk-basis preconditioners can work without training for constant-coefficient problems, while energy-norm training can improve performance for high-contrast coefficients.
engineering_relevance: Matching neural coarse spaces and training losses to solver physics can reduce conjugate gradient iterations in heterogeneous elasticity simulations.
method: Build two-level Schwarz coarse spaces from DeepONet trunk functions restricted to subdomains.
Prove that untrained trunk spans approximate low-degree polynomial spaces in 1D under nondegeneracy assumptions.
Compare untrained, ℓ²-trained, energy-trained, and equal-dimension piecewise polynomial coarse spaces.
evidence_signal: Poisson and 3D elasticity tests show similar iteration counts for untrained and polynomial spaces with constant coefficients; energy-trained spaces outperform polynomials for Poisson at contrast 10⁵ and, with rigid-body enrichment, achieve the fewest iterations at larger coarse dimensions for an optimized elastic cantilever at contrast 10⁶.
watch_item: The theoretical result is limited to 1D under suitable assumptions, and fewer solver iterations do not by themselves establish an end-to-end speedup after training costs.
paper_title: Do DeepONet Trunk-Basis Preconditioners Need Training?
